title: Chikungunya: acute, subacute and chronic (India, NCVBDC)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Fever with severe symmetrical polyarthralgia. Acute phase: rest, fluids and paracetamol, no NSAIDs until dengue is excluded and no steroids. Subacute phase: NSAIDs, short prednisolone course for severe synovitis. Chronic phase beyond 3 months: hydroxychloroquine and other DMARDs with rheumatology input.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Abrupt high fever lasting 3 to 5 days with severe, often disabling, symmetrical polyarthralgia of the small peripheral joints (hands, wrists, ankles), sometimes knees and shoulders; rash on day 2 to 5 in some; myalgia, headache.
Phases: acute (under 3 weeks), subacute (3 weeks to 3 months), chronic (beyond 3 months).

Atypical or severe forms (rare, more in infants, elderly and comorbid patients): encephalitis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, myelitis, optic neuritis, myocarditis, arrhythmia, uveitis, AKI, hepatitis, bullous skin lesions in infants, neonatal encephalopathy.

Differentiate from dengue: chikungunya is arthralgia-predominant with less bleeding, shock and thrombocytopenia, but co-infection occurs; organ dysfunction should prompt a search for co-infection (dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, scrub typhus).
High risk for complications: age under 1 year or over 65, pregnancy near term, diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, COPD, chronic kidney or liver disease.

sections.title: Investigations
items: RT-PCR for CHIKV RNA in the first week (day 0 to 7); IgM ELISA (MAC-ELISA) after day 7. IgM may persist for months, so interpret with the clinical picture.
CBC and dengue NS1 or IgM plus malaria smear or RDT in every case, as treatment differs.
Subacute or chronic joint symptoms: ESR, CRP, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP and uric acid to exclude other arthritides; X-ray of affected joints if persistent.

sections.title: Acute phase (first 3 weeks)
items: No antiviral exists; treat symptomatically. Rest, adequate fluids, cold compresses to joints, gentle exercise during recovery.
Paracetamol: adults 500 mg 3 to 4 times daily (NCVBDC maximum 3 g/day); children 10 to 15 mg/kg per dose 6-hourly.
Step 2 for adults if paracetamol fails: tramadol 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 400 mg/day (300 mg/day over 75 years). Avoid opioids in children.
No NSAIDs or aspirin in the acute phase, and never before dengue is excluded (WHO 2025 strong recommendation against NSAIDs in acute arboviral disease); in children none in the first 14 days.
No corticosteroids in the acute phase. Avoid self-medication with antibiotics or other analgesics.

sections.title: Subacute phase (3 weeks to 3 months)
items: Assess pain score (VAS), number of tender and swollen joints, morning stiffness, CRP and ESR.

Mild pain (VAS 1 to 3): NSAID at full anti-inflammatory dose with gastroprotection; review at 1 week, change class if inadequate by day 10, and taper (alternate days for 1 to 2 weeks) before stopping.
Oral steroid for severe polyarticular synovitis or tenosynovitis, VAS 4 to 10, or NSAID failure or contraindication: prednisolone 10 mg/day for 5 days, then taper over 10 days.

Severe presentations: prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg/day until walking unaided and pain controlled, continue 3 to 5 days after full resolution, then reduce by 5 mg/day every 7 days. Do not exceed 4 weeks in total.
Local steroid injection for tenosynovitis, bursitis or synovitis not controlled orally. No DMARDs before 8 weeks.

sections.title: Chronic phase (beyond 3 months)
items: Distinguish post-chikungunya chronic inflammatory rheumatism (new inflammatory arthritis with confirmed CHIKV serology and other causes excluded) from non-inflammatory musculoskeletal disorders.
Mild: paracetamol then NSAIDs; moderate to severe: short steroid course if not used before, using the subacute regimen.
DMARDs are the mainstay for moderate to severe inflammatory disease: hydroxychloroquine up to 6.5 mg/kg/day (usually 400 mg/day) for 8 to 12 weeks with an NSAID.
Inadequate response after 8 to 12 weeks: methotrexate, sulfasalazine or leflunomide under a physician experienced in their use; refer persistent inflammatory arthritis to rheumatology.
Physiotherapy and rehabilitation for function; screen for low mood.

sections.title: Pregnancy, neonates and comorbidities
items: Pregnancy: paracetamol only, no NSAIDs; involve obstetrics near term. Transmission to the baby is highest when delivery falls in the maternal viraemic window (about 1 day before to 5 days after onset of maternal fever); caesarean section does not prevent it.
Neonates infected around birth present at day 3 to 7 with fever, poor feeding, rash, seizures or encephalopathy; consider echocardiography and follow neurodevelopment.
Infants: fever, seizures, diarrhoea, oedema, vesiculobullous rash and peeling; arthritis is uncommon. Admit and monitor.
Diabetes: glycaemic control may worsen; monitor closely and consider early insulin. Hypertension: a fall in MAP of 40 mmHg from baseline indicates hypotension; avoid aggressive BP lowering.

sections.title: Refer or admit
items: Atypical manifestations, neurological or respiratory deterioration, organ dysfunction, hypotension, or worsening vital signs.
Infants, pregnant women with contractions or abnormal fetal heart rate, and high-risk patients who cannot maintain oral intake.
Persistent inflammatory arthritis beyond 3 months: rheumatology.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving NSAIDs for joint pain before dengue is excluded.
Starting steroids in the acute phase, or continuing them beyond 4 weeks.
Diagnosing on IgM alone in a patient with chronic arthritis without excluding rheumatoid arthritis or gout.
Missing co-infection when a 'chikungunya' patient develops organ dysfunction.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: Adults 500 mg orally 3 to 4 times daily (maximum 3 g/day per NCVBDC); children 10 to 15 mg/kg per dose 6-hourly
drugs.notes: First line in the acute phase and in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Tramadol
drugs.dose: Adults 50 to 100 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 400 mg/day (300 mg/day over 75 years)
drugs.notes: Step 2 when paracetamol fails. Not in children.

drugs.name: Ibuprofen (children)
drugs.notes: Only after the first 14 days of illness and once dengue is excluded.

drugs.name: Naproxen (children)
drugs.dose: 10 to 15 mg/kg/day orally in 2 divided doses
drugs.notes: Only after the first 14 days of illness.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.dose: 10 mg/day for 5 days then taper over 10 days; severe disease 0.5 mg/kg/day, then reduce by 5 mg/day every 7 days after resolution
drugs.notes: Subacute or chronic inflammatory disease only; maximum 4 weeks. Never in the acute phase.

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.dose: Up to 6.5 mg/kg/day orally (usually 400 mg/day) for 8 to 12 weeks
drugs.notes: Chronic inflammatory arthritis, with an NSAID. Baseline eye assessment for long-term use.
